# 01 — Shared lifecycle abstractions and traits

## Outcome

Implement a shared abstract waypoint model and small lifecycle-state vocabulary
for Mission, Waypoint, and Ticket adapters, with optional lifecycle behaviors
as separate traits/capabilities. Ticket-backed status remains read from the
Ticket and is never replaced by a Mission-owned duplicate.

## Non-goal

Do not add a generic workflow backend/store, alter Ticket history, or expose
new MCP transport.

## Inputs and implementation boundary

Use the approved [Mission Domain spec](../../workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/spec/specs/38a8ea3a-9a6a-4a0f-bc5a-97dc9ba670fc/spec.toml),
[Ticket feature schema](../../workflow-tools/ticket/crates/ticket-api/schemas/feature.toml),
and [settled design](ARTIFACTS.md#settled-design-notes-proposals-not-current-apis).
Make unsupported mappings explicit; specifically do not inherit the existing
`cancelled -> blocked` projection as the desired semantic model.

Define `planned`, `active`, `paused`, `blocked`, `completed`, and `cancelled`
as the shared basic projection, while retaining each domain's native
state/revision. Ticket `planning`/`ready` project to planned; its implementation
and review states project to active; blocked/on-hold/terminal mappings retain
their distinct meaning. Expose read/transition through domain adapters, not
a second writable Ticket state field. A Mission is a lifecycle-capable
container of abstract waypoints, not itself a fabricated Ticket.

Capabilities remain separate: planning edits, pause/resume, cancellation,
completion/result review, revision approval, Session handoff and reopening.
Unsupported capability queries return an explicit result, not a no-op.
Reuse an existing dependency-safe shared contract owner if one exists;
otherwise a small shared type/trait crate is allowed, but never a shared
entity database or registry. Domain persistence stays in its current store.

## Expected post-state and validation

Concrete domain types and trait tests represent common simple state and
separately compose revision/approval/pause/handoff/cancel/completion/reopen
capabilities. Ticket-backed adapters prove Ticket status is authoritative.

Future target (not existing evidence): `cd workflow-tools && cargo test -p mission`.

## Checkpoint

Commit the domain model and tests only after the target passes.

fields.__previous_part_content__:
Implement [the authoritative contract](../../../../spec/specs/908e1755-d486-4e49-8b63-3f9eee81396e/body.md), criteria MN-W1-01 through MN-W1-04, using the [execution package](../../../../../../transcripts/29-10-2026_mission-native-mcp-planning/01-shared-lifecycle-abstractions.md).

Owning code: mission/crates/mission-api/src/lib.rs, mission/crates/mission/src/lib.rs, ticket/crates/ticket-api/src/lib.rs.

Example: A cancelled linked Ticket projects cancelled, not blocked. An on-hold Ticket projects paused. Querying an unsupported reopen capability returns an explicit unsupported-capability result without changing either store.

Failure boundary: Unknown state, absent foreign authority and unsupported capability are explicit errors. No Ticket history mutation, automatic native-state migration or new shared entity registry.

Non-goal: Session intake, named MCP transport, generic entity storage and Ticket reopening.

Checkpoint after G1 shared-lifecycle: `feat(workflow): add shared lifecycle capability contracts`. Provider criteria and entry/exit conditions are linked in the execution package; a passed predecessor checkpoint and explicit execution approval are required before activation.
